0.text: Former defence secretary and CIA director Leon Panetta told the Guardian that the Pentagon is taking a "shameful approach" to releasing information about US casualties in the Iran war.
The US Defence Department has not held a press briefing for two-and-a-half months.
A fragile ceasefire between the US and Iran collapsed earlier in July 2026, leading to daily strikes between both sides.
The number of US troops killed in the war on Iran rose to 18, while roughly 430 US troops have been injured.
The Pentagon stated on Monday that 100 service members had been injured since 7 July, but 96% had returned to duty.
Pentagon spokesperson Sean Parnell blamed a temporary data disruption for a website update that temporarily lowered the US troop death count from 18 to 14.
In October, most news outlets turned in their access badges and walked out of the Pentagon over new rules requiring pre-approval from Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth.
The pro-Iranian account Iran Army Media shared a video on X on July 19 claiming to show an Iranian missile downing an American B-52 bomber.
Fact-checking outlet Lead Stories reported that the viral video showing a B-52 bomber being shot down was likely taken from a military flight simulator or video game.
Ansarollah media said on Telegram early on Saturday that a Yemeni missile strike caused fires in the Saudi city of Jizan.
Saudi Arabia launched air strikes on Houthi targets in the Yemeni port city of Hodeida and a nearby island on Friday.
The US military carried out 13 consecutive nights of attacks on Iran prior to Saturday.
US Navy Captain Tim Hawkins stated that US forces disabled a tanker ship in the Gulf of Oman that was attempting to evade the American blockade on Iranian ports.
In June, the US and Iran agreed on a 14-point Memorandum of Understanding to halt military operations and reopen the Strait of Hormuz.
Yemen's Iran-backed Houthi rebels announced an immediate maritime embargo against Saudi Arabia in the Bab al-Mandeb Strait.
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said pressure on Tehran would continue, stating: "The price will continue to get higher every single night until they come to their senses."
US Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth stated that the cost of the ongoing conflict with Iran had reached $37.5 billion.
Saudi authorities issued emergency warnings for the provinces of Jazan and Yanbu around 6:10 a.m. local time on Saturday.
Brent crude oil soared around 27% in two weeks, closing on Friday at $96.78 a barrel.

1.text: An additional 25,000 people were evacuated from villages near Madrid threatened by wildfires, bringing the total evacuated there to 70,000.
More than 250,000 people have been evacuated across France and Spain due to ongoing wildfires.
The French government stated that 197,000 people were evacuated because of wildfires near Bordeaux.
A wildfire in Scotland's Cairngorms national park has been burning for 11 days.
European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen announced that 5 planes and 2 helicopters from the rescEU fleet were deployed to France.
The Spanish government ordered the evacuation of the entire Tiétar Valley in the province of Ávila, affecting 30,000 people.
According to EFFIS data, 69,473 hectares of land have burned in France since the start of the year, setting a record high for land burned in a single year.
Carlos Novillo, Madrid regional government's emergency management chief, stated that the wildfire near the capital was at its peak and beyond the capacity of firefighters to contain.
Spain's interior ministry reported that wildfires burned nearly 10,000 hectares in the Madrid region and between 13,000 and 15,000 hectares in Ávila.
Around 44,000 people fled the Cap Ferret peninsula south of Bordeaux, where more than 50 houses have been destroyed.
French Interior Minister Laurent Nunez stated that wildfires across France have burned nearly 98,000 hectares.
The Spanish government declared a national emergency as wildfires burned out of control in several areas.
Wildfires in southwest France forced around 200,000 people to evacuate.

2.text: Regional governor Yevgeny Balitsky stated that a suspected Ukrainian attack on holiday camps in Russian-held Zaporizhia killed at least eight people, including two children.
Three drivers for private Ukrainian postal service Nova Poshta were killed when a Russian drone struck a facility in the Sumy region.
Romanian President Nicusor Dan stated that a Romanian F-16 pilot safely shot down a drone breaching Romanian airspace near the Ukrainian border.
A Russian attack on a site hosting a defence industry event near Kyiv killed at least 10 people and wounded nearly 100 others.
Five people were killed by Russian glide bombs in the eastern Ukrainian city of Sloviansk.
A Ukrainian strike on Friday killed six people and wounded 26 in the Russian city of Kirov.
Ukrainian forces attacked warehouses belonging to Wildberries, Russia's largest online retailer, in St Petersburg.
Ukrainian air force spokesman Yuri Ihnat stated that three ballistic missiles were used in the attack near Kyiv, with only one intercepted.
Acting regional military administration head Ruslan Oliinyk stated that the strike hit a private military training site in the Bucha district, 20 to 30 kilometers from central Kyiv.
EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas reported that a strike in Sloviansk hit Latvia's Honorary Consulate.
Ukrainian energy company Ukrenergo reported that around 150,000 people were left without power in the Chernihiv region after an attack on an energy facility.

3.text: A family in the occupied West Bank rescued a baby from a house set on fire by Israeli settlers following a shootout.
Palestinians in the village of Tell held a funeral early Saturday for four men killed in a clash with Israeli settlers, with the Israeli army restricting attendance to about 30 people.
The Israeli military stated that a Palestinian villager in Tell seized an Israeli's weapon and shot one settler dead, sparking gunfire that left four Palestinians and a second Israeli dead.
Farata local council head Abdel Moneim Shanneh said settlers set fire to olive groves and the Israeli army fired on villagers trying to extinguish the flames.
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu ordered the establishment of new settler outposts and accelerated legalisation of farm outposts in the occupied West Bank.
According to Palestinian health ministry data, Israeli soldiers or settlers have killed at least 1,094 Palestinians since the start of the Gaza war.
At least four Palestinians and two Israelis were killed in a shooting incident in the West Bank village of Tal.
The Israeli military stated that a 27-year-old Israeli soldier fell during operational activity in the area of Tal village.
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Defence Minister Israel Katz issued a joint statement confirming the shooter's home in Tal would be demolished.
Israeli forces arrested nearly 50 Palestinians and raided roughly 70 homes in the village of Tal following Friday's shooting.
UN Special Rapporteur Francesca Albanese described Israeli attacks on Palestinian civilians across the West Bank as "pogroms" and called for an immediate arms embargo on Israel.
The Palestinian Health Ministry stated that at least 87 Palestinians have been killed by Israelis in the West Bank since the beginning of 2026, including 21 by settlers.

4.text: Member states of the International Criminal Court voted by a large majority to remove chief prosecutor Karim Khan following sexual misconduct allegations.
Karim Khan is the first chief prosecutor ever to be removed from office in the International Criminal Court's history.
Assembly of States Parties president Päivi Kaukoranta announced that Karim Khan had committed serious misconduct and serious breach of duty.
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio announced that the United States is launching a sweeping campaign to dismantle the International Criminal Court.
Foreign Affairs Minister Félix Plasencia announced that Venezuela will withdraw from the International Criminal Court.
Israel's UN ambassador Danny Danon stated that Karim Khan launched a political witch hunt against Israel to hide sexual misconduct allegations.
The decision to remove Karim Khan passed with 82 votes in favour during a Special Session of the Assembly of States Parties.
Karim Khan's lawyer stated he would challenge the lawfulness and fairness of the removal decision through all available legal mechanisms.
Karim Khan was unable to attend the vote at UN headquarters in New York because he is barred from entering the US under Trump administration sanctions.
An investigation by the UN Office of Internal Oversight Services into Karim Khan ran from November 2024 to December 2025 and generated over 5,000 pages of evidence.

5.text: Protesters in Kyiv announced an open-ended rally demanding President Volodymyr Zelensky reappoint ousted defence minister Mykhailo Fedorov.
President Volodymyr Zelensky decided on 15 July not to reappoint Mykhailo Fedorov as defence minister during a cabinet reshuffle.

Mykhailo Fedorov said he rejected Zelensky's offers of alternative government posts, saying: "there were only three positions worth having to influence the course of the war: minister of defence, commander-in-chief of the military or president of Ukraine."
President Volodymyr Zelensky appointed 43-year-old Maj Gen Mykhailo Drapatyi as commander-in-chief of Ukraine's military, replacing Oleksandr Syrskyi.
Ukrainian MP Oleksandr Merezhko stated that Mykhailo Fedorov's public rating soared following his removal from office.

6.text: SpaceX's 122-metre-tall Starship rocket completed a test flight and splashed down intact in the Indian Ocean.
SpaceX head Elon Musk stated on X: "Starship is intact, floating in the ocean and transmitting telemetry!"
During its test flight, Starship deployed 20 upgraded Starlink V3 internet satellites into suborbital space.
NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman commented that Starship's capabilities will be game-changing and ensure humanity never gives up the Moon again.
SpaceX launched its 13th Starship test flight from Texas on Friday after being rescheduled twice this month.
Starship blasted off around 6:50 p.m. Eastern Time from Starbase in Texas.
Five engines on the Super Heavy booster failed to reignite during descent, causing it to strike the Gulf of Mexico with greater force than intended.
SpaceX aims to use Starship to expand its Starlink network with V3 satellites by the end of the year to allow standard cell phones to connect directly to satellite service.

7.text: US President Donald Trump threatened the European Union with steep tariffs and a trade investigation after Brussels fined Google $1 billion over antitrust violations.
US President Donald Trump wrote on social media that penalties against US tech firms are "highly unethical" and that the US "is not a 'PIGGYBANK' for Europe".
The European Commission fined Google $1 billion for breaching the Digital Markets Act by favouring its own services in search results and restricting app developers.
European Commission Executive Vice President Teresa Ribera called the penalty against Google "decisive yet balanced".
Google executive Kent Walker described the EU ruling as "product degradation" driven by a small number of complainants.
Donald Trump announced the US will immediately initiate a Section 301 investigation into European regulators' practices regarding American tech firms.
Donald Trump claimed Apple received $15 billion in EU fines, Meta received $3 billion, and Amazon received $2.5 billion.
Trump posted on Truth Social that the European Union "will pay a very big price" and anticipated placing a substantial tariff on the bloc.
EU courts recently upheld a record fine of over $4 billion against Google following an eight-year review process.

8.text: Protesters celebrated at Jantar Mantar after Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan resigned from his post on Saturday.
Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan resigned following weeks of nationwide protests over alleged irregularities in competitive examinations.
The Cockroach Janta Party announced it was withdrawing its agitation in good faith following Pradhan's resignation and agreement on key terms.
Dharmendra Pradhan stated he submitted his resignation to Prime Minister Narendra Modi so that "anti-national forces" do not take advantage of ongoing protests.
Delhi Police used lathis, tear gas, and pellet guns against demonstrators during a march to Parliament on Monday, injuring dozens.
Cockroach Janata Party founder Abhijeet Dipke called Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation "a victory for democracy" and "a victory for the Constitution of India".
Abhijeet Dipke demanded one crore rupees in compensation for the families of students who committed suicide over exam irregularities.
Dharmendra Pradhan announced that future NEET examinations would be conducted as Computer-Based Tests to enhance transparency.
Activist Sonam Wangchuk observed a 26-day hunger strike as part of the protests demanding accountability over examination leaks.
Union Minister J.P. Nadda confirmed the government will take steps to withdraw FIRs against peaceful protesters and provide financial compensation to families of NEET suicide victims.
